newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Roche not borrowing for takeover - analysts.
newsitem.headline: Roche not borrowing for takeover - analysts.

text.p: A billion dollar convertible note scheme reportedly launched by Roche Holding AG probably reflects the company's thirst for cheap liquidity rather than any move to stock up its bulging war chest, analysts said.
"An extra billion dollars is hardly likely to have any impact on any sizeable acquisition. This is peanuts," said Genghis Lloyd-Harris at CSFB in London.
"Are they raising the money to do an acquisition? Almost certainly not."

Swiss stock traders also played down the prospect that Roche was preparing for a takeover by topping up the 15 billion Swiss francs it already has on hand, but shares of France's Synthelabo and other pharmaceutical firms rose on such talk.

"Roche does not have to tap capital markets at all to finance a takeover," one Swiss stock trader said. With around 15 billion Swiss francs in securities and liquid assets, Roche had more than enough money to buy a company like Synthelabo," he said.
"Roche is simply taking advantage of the favourable environment to raise money," another dealer said. "There does not have to be a takeover in the background."
"They did make a point at their analysts presentation that they will continue to raise money whenever they can...at very cheap rates and continue to invest it," he said.
Roche has done seven previous financings on an opportunistic basis to raise money at low rates and invest it.

"Last year they earned something like a 15.3 percent pre-tax return on their total cash and marketable securities. That is very impressive. So if they can raise money at a very low rate...and can get that sort of return on it, it is a very sensible thing to so," he said.
Some Swiss traders suggested Roche's cash pile was a good reason for the company to make a purchase.
"They are forced to so something," one dealer said. "People don't want to pay high P/Es for a company that is one-third a bank."

Lloyd-Harris said he and other analysts would rather see Roche hand back some of the cash to shareholders, but added company officials have made clear they see the chance to make a handsome return on their liquid assets.
Roche is often rumoured to be in the market for a takeover, but this talk has died down a bit of late.

"It became very clear from the announcements they made with their first-quarter earnings that they have a lot to focus on in improving the operations of their current pharmaceutical business and in drug launches," Lloyd-Harris said.

"I don't think they are going to go out and do a major acquisition...I still think if they could find something in the $5 billion to $15 billion range they would do it, but such opportunities are few and far between."
Roche officials could not be reached for comment. A spokesman reiterated earlier that Roche does not comment on market rumours.
